predecessors.note: Fuladu was founded in 1867 "after the Battle of Kansala" by Alpha Molo; the infobox lists Kaabu as the preceding state and many provinces were "former Kaabu kingdoms reorganized under Fulbe leaders".

"The British annexed their section into the Gambia Colony and Protectorate in 1902" (Musa Molo page).

capitals.name: Ndorna
capitals.note: "In 1874 he established his capital in Ndorna, north of Kolda." The infobox also lists Hamdallaye, where a French resident was stationed (1901). The page gives no coordinates; the point is the researcher's approximation north of the gazetteer's Kolda (not in the gazetteer).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Fuladu row). Founded 1867 after the Battle of Kansala by Alpha Molo; the page places Fuladu in the upper Casamance (Kolda is the reference point for the capital), extending to parts of the Gambia and Guinea-Bissau; campaigns reached the Gambia River; two Gambian districts, Fulladu West and Fulladu East, carry the name. The shape is the same Kolda, Upper River and Central River region the kaabu dossier gives Fuladu at its breakaway. The 1900 division of Fuladu into British and French spheres changes no claim until 1902.

keyframe_review.note: 1902: "The British annexed their section into the Gambia Colony and Protectorate"; the Senegalese (French) part under Musa Molo is the Kolda region until May 1903, when he fled with about 3,000 people to the British side.

ledger.note: 1867: Fuladu is founded. Infobox "Established 1867"; the page: founded "after the Battle of Kansala, which captured the Mandinka capital in an 11-day fight". The month follows the kaabu dossier (13-24 May 1867 at Kansala, Battle of Kansala page).

region.text: Fuladu, 'in the upper Casamance region of southern Senegal, extending to parts of The Gambia', as the Kolda region and the Gambian Upper River and Central River (the page also reaches 'northeastern Guinea-Bissau', which is Futa Jallon land in the kaabu dossier and is not drawn here)

ledger.note: May 1867: Fuladu takes the upper Casamance and Gambia lands from Kaabu. The page: "overthrowing Mandinka supremacy... many of its provinces were former Kaabu kingdoms reorganized under Fulbe leaders"; the kaabu dossier has the loss at Kansala in May 1867.
1874: Alpha Molo moves the capital. "In 1874 he established his capital in Ndorna, north of Kolda."

1902: the British annex their section. The Musa Molo page: Fuladu was divided into spheres of influence "in 1900" and "The British annexed their section into the Gambia Colony and Protectorate" in 1902 (no month). The Gambian districts Fulladu West and East carry the name.

region.text: the French sphere of Fuladu round Kolda and Ndorna, which Musa Molo held until May 1903

ledger.note: May 1903: Musa Molo leaves the French sphere. "In May 1903 the French attempted to bring Musa to heel"; instead he led about 3,000 people to the British side, and the page says Fuladu "ceased to exist as an independent power".

region.text: the French sphere of Fuladu round Kolda and Ndorna, which Musa Molo held until May 1903

ledger.note: 1903: the last independent pre-colonial state in the area ends. "It was the last independent pre-colonial state in the area, ceasing to exist in 1903." (infobox: disestablished 1903). Musa Molo was exiled to The Gambia and later to Sierra Leone (1919).

notes:
Fuladu, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Pages: Fuladu, Musa Molo, Battle of Kansala.

The founding month follows the kaabu dossier (Battle of Kansala page, 13-24 May 1867); the Fuladu page itself gives only 1867. The 1900 division into French and British spheres of influence changed no claim until the British annexation of 1902 (no month on the page); the French resident accepted by Musa Molo at Hamdallaye in 1901, with half his tax revenue conceded, is a protectorate step for the french-africa ledger (vassal_start 1901, vassal_end 1903). The Fuladu page also extends the state to "northeastern Guinea-Bissau", which the kaabu dossier gives to the Futa Jallon imamate; the Fuladu shape here stays with Kolda and the two Gambian regions. Musa Molo's two invasions of Kantora (Musa Molo page) are undated and not in the ledger. Capital Ndorna and Hamdallaye are not in the gazetteer.
